pages.label: QA-01
pages.title: Computational Problems, Promises, and Cost Models
pages.summary: Define finite computational tasks as encoded promise relations and distinguish exact from worst-case bounded-error correctness. Reuse the root promise-problem and promise-reduction contracts, and specialize the QC coherent-function-oracle and uniform-circuit interfaces to the query model. Count oracle calls separately from non-oracle quantum gates and classical bit operations; define expected query cost from finite execution prefixes and distinguish it from a worst-case cap. State which resources include input preparation, measurement, random coins, and query-independent computation; any nonzero initialized state must have an explicit access or preparation model and its cost is charged. The A page must make explicit that a bare oracle or matrix does not provide a cheaper gate implementation, controlled access, or state preparation.

pages.label: QA-01B
pages.title: Computational Problems, Promises, and Cost Models — Examples
pages.summary: Worked examples compare total and promise tasks, promise-preserving reductions, oracle calls, circuit gates and classical bit cost. This companion is a logical leaf.

pages.label: QA-02
pages.title: Reversible Arithmetic and Oracle Conversion
pages.summary: Specialize the QC coherent function-oracle and reversible-embedding contracts without redefining them. Prove phase kickback and the one-query bit-to-phase conversion; prepare the fixed |−⟩ target explicitly with X then H from zero and charge those gates. The reverse conversion explicitly assumes controlled phase-oracle access. Specify compute-copy-uncompute with clean workspace and its forward/copy/inverse cost, and define the coherent XOR dot-product arithmetic used later. Preserve the distinction between a global phase on an uncontrolled state and a relative phase made observable by control.

pages.label: QA-02B
pages.title: Reversible Arithmetic and Oracle Conversion — Examples
pages.summary: Finite examples check phase kickback, clean and unclean workspace, XOR arithmetic, and why bare phase access does not automatically supply controlled access. This companion is a logical leaf.

pages.label: QA-03
pages.title: Exact Oracle Algorithms
pages.summary: State the one-bit Deutsch promise, the n-bit constant-versus-balanced Deutsch–Jozsa promise, and the no-offset Bernstein–Vazirani inner-product promise. Give exact one-query circuit instructions from zero initialization, including the X then H target preparation and charged one-qubit gate counts, and prove output distributions from the F2 Hadamard character sum. Compare deterministic exact query counts with randomized bounded-error costs precisely; do not claim an exponential bounded-error classical lower bound for Deutsch–Jozsa.

pages.label: QA-03B
pages.title: Exact Oracle Algorithms — Examples
pages.summary: Small Deutsch, Deutsch–Jozsa and Bernstein–Vazirani truth tables check the exact promises, the zero-frequency measurement rule, and the distinction between exact and bounded-error classical query cost. This companion is a logical leaf.

pages.label: QA-04
pages.title: Simon’s Algorithm and Finite-Field Recovery
pages.summary: Specify Simon’s nonzero XOR-period promise, derive the two-preimage coset state and the uniform sample from s-perp by a direct F2 Hadamard calculation, then recover s from n−1 independent rows. Use the exact rank-growth probability to prove almost-sure termination, expected O(n) queries, and a bounded-round failure branch using Markov’s inequality. State and prove the classical randomized Ω(2^(n/2)) oracle lower bound under an explicit random-instance distribution and query model.

pages.label: QA-04B
pages.title: Simon’s Algorithm and Finite-Field Recovery — Examples
pages.summary: Worked n=1 and n=2 cases expose the zero-row boundary, the unique nonzero kernel vector, the exact rank-rise probabilities and the Gaussian-elimination output. This companion is a logical leaf.

pages.label: QA-05
pages.title: Finite Abelian Fourier Analysis
pages.summary: Reuse the root additive-character definition, proved character-value and row-orthogonality results, finite abelian invariant-factor classification, and cyclic Fourier page. Add the missing dual group, cyclic/product character counts, dual-index orthogonality, general normalized transform, inversion, Parseval, convolution normalization, and annihilator/double-annihilator identities with exact finite proofs. Fix the convention as |G|^(-1/2) times the negative-character sum and make the sqrt(|G|) convolution factor explicit.

pages.label: QA-05B
pages.title: Finite Abelian Fourier Analysis — Examples
pages.summary: Character tables of cyclic groups and products check dual cardinality, orthogonality, Parseval, convolution normalization and subgroup annihilators. This companion is a logical leaf.

pages.label: QA-06
pages.title: Quantum Fourier-Transform Circuits
pages.summary: Define the positive-sign cyclic QFT as the inverse of the root negative-sign DFT. Derive the binary product factorization and exact H/controlled-phase circuit with output register order and final bit-reversal swaps. Prove the O(n^2) ideal-rotation count and the operator-norm telescoping error for omitting rotations with denominator index s>m; choose m from n and target ε to obtain O(n log(n/ε)) ideal gates when m<n. Give a separate fixed-gate-set compile count from the QC11/QC12 exact decomposition and Solovay–Kitaev compiler; the statement is in gate count, not classical target-angle bit-time.

pages.label: QA-06B
pages.title: Quantum Fourier-Transform Circuits — Examples
pages.summary: The N=4 and N=8 circuits check sign, tensor order, bit reversal, exact gate counts and an explicit truncation-error parameter. This companion is a logical leaf.
